issues.failure_explanation: The sampling map is non-injective, and equality of sampled functions does not imply equality of their sampled images under $\Aa$. Thus $\sum_i c_i\wh{\psi}_i=0$ need not imply $\sum_i c_i\widehat{\Aa\psi_i}=0$, so the purported induced operator $\wh{\Aa}$ is not defined on empirical equivalence classes. The proof's final equality assumes precisely this unproved implication. For example, with one sample, two dictionary functions both taking value 1 there, but their $\Aa$-images taking values 1 and -1, the coefficient relation $(1,-1)$ represents zero empirically while its image does not.

failure_location.quote: Then the matrix $\wh{\bm{A}}_{NM}$ which approximates $\wh{\Aa}$ is, with probability $1$, a matrix representation of the projection of $\wh{\Aa}$ onto $\wh{\Ff}_{NM}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the sampling kernel to be invariant under the sampled action of $\Aa$, or restrict to the regime where the sampled dictionary is linearly independent and define the operator through that identification. The latter withdraws the advertised projection result for singular empirical Gram matrices.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed projection interpretation without invertibility and the first equality in the exact-approximation corollary are not meaningful or valid in general.
issues.title: The empirical operator is not well-defined on the empirical quotient space

issues.failure_explanation: Continuity across cell interfaces couples local degrees of freedom, so the global dimension is not the number of cells times $k^d$. Moreover, polynomials of degree up to $k$ in each variable have $(k+1)^d$ local coefficients before continuity constraints, not $k^d$. Consequently, choosing $k^d$ independent nodes per disjoint cell does not generally yield unique continuous nodal basis functions.

Its first term is $\varepsilon\|f\|_{\Dd}$, not bounded by the stated $\|\Aa\|\|f\|_{\Dd}\varepsilon$ when $\|\Aa\|<1$, and the projection term carries another unspecified approximation constant. The displayed $\lesssim$ conclusion therefore does not prove the exact probability bound in the theorem.

The displayed formula would give zero sample complexity when $C_N=0$, even though empirical cross-covariance can fluctuate whenever $T_N\ne0$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The random variables $\set{(\bm{\eta}_N^m, \bm{\xi}_N^m)}_{m=1}^M$ have mean $\bm{0}$, are symmetric, independent, and independent of $\set{\bm{x}_m }_{m=1}^M$.

issues.failure_explanation: Zero mean removes linear cross terms but not quadratic noise covariance: $\mathbb E[(\Psi+\eta)(\Psi+\eta)^\dagger]=G_N+\mathbb E[\eta\eta^\dagger]$. Likewise, $\mathbb E[(\Aa\Psi+\xi)(\Psi+\eta)^\dagger]=C_N+\mathbb E[\xi\eta^\dagger]$, which need not equal $C_N$ because the assumption does not require $\xi$ and $\eta$ to be mutually uncorrelated. Hence Bernstein concentration is applied around the wrong matrices, and the noisy estimator generally has persistent errors-in-variables bias.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must debias the empirical Gram and cross matrices using known noise covariances, adopt an errors-in-variables estimator, or weaken the conclusion to include a nonvanishing bias term.
issues.overall_effect: The noisy estimator is not shown to converge to $\Aa_N$; its claimed error bound can tend to zero while the estimator converges to a biased population operator.
issues.title: Centered additive noise does not leave the Gram and structure matrices unbiased
issues.why_classification: The central noisy-convergence guarantee fails even with arbitrarily many samples and requires a different estimator or a materially weaker error guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The conditioning event bounds every one of the $M$ independent noise vectors. Its probability is $(\tl p_N)^M$, not $\tl p_N$. Therefore the valid relation is $(\tl p_N)^M\tl{\mathbb P}(A)\leq\mathbb P(A)$, and the claimed confidence estimate with $p<\tl p_N$ does not follow. For fixed $\tl p_N<1$, the probability of the conditioning event actually decreases to zero as $M$ grows.

issues.failure_explanation: The squared norm of the combined $2N$-dimensional Gaussian vector divided by $\sigma^2$ has a $\chi^2_{2N}$ distribution, not the displayed $\chi^2_N$ law. The probability of being below a threshold is a CDF, not $1-F_N$, and the displayed upper bound is then used to conclude an incompatible lower bound. At the chosen threshold $2N\sigma^2$, equal to the mean of $\chi^2_{2N}$, the probability is not close to one.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the $\chi^2_{2N}$ CDF with a threshold chosen above its mean and recompute the resulting truncation probability and noise factor; the claimed near-one probability at the stated threshold must be withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The first part follows from $\left(\lambda_{NM}\right)$ and $\big(f_{NM}\big)$ being bounded sequences of $\C$ and $\Ff_N\subset \Dd$, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: The norms of the finite-dimensional operators may grow with $N$, especially because the framework expressly permits unbounded $\Aa$. Individual boundedness of every $\Aa_N$ gives no uniform bound on $\lambda_N$. For example, on $\ell^2$ take the closed diagonal operator $\Aa e_n=n e_n$, $\Ff_N=\operatorname{span}(e_1,\ldots,e_N)$, and the normalized eigenfunction $f_N=e_N/\|e_N\|_{\Dd}$. Then $\lambda_N=N$ has no convergent subsequence, while the projection assumption holds.

failure_location.quote: Additionally, for each $N$, $\Aa_N$ is bounded. Thus, the sequence of eigenvalues $(\lambda_{N})$ is also bounded and has a convergent subsequence.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a uniform bound on the selected eigenvalues or on the Galerkin operators, or state the result only for an a priori bounded spectral window. This excludes general arbitrary eigenpair sequences for unbounded generators.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted existence of convergent eigenvalue subsequences in both dictionary and joint limits fails for operators explicitly allowed by the paper.
issues.title: Boundedness of each Galerkin operator does not bound a sequence of selected eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: Repair requires changing a central spectral quantifier or excluding an important advertised class of unbounded operators.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\big(\lambda_{N_i,M_i},f_{N_i,M_i}\big)$ be such a convergent sequence and suppose that Assumptions \ref{assumption}, \ref{moments assumption}, \ref{projection assumption}, and \ref{projection operator assumption} hold.

issues.failure_explanation: Selecting a convergent subsequence at the particular indices $(N_i,M_{N_i})$ gives no convergence for an arbitrarily prescribed eigenpair from every larger $M'_{N_i}$. Even for a constant operator with two eigenvalues, the indexed eigenpair family may select one eigenvalue for even $M$ and the other for odd $M$; after any thresholds, an allowed choice of $M'_{N_i}$ can force either branch. Operator convergence does not canonically match arbitrary eigenpair labels across sample sizes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the universal statement by existence of a jointly chosen diagonal subsequence of eigenpairs, or impose spectral isolation and a consistent spectral projection or branch-selection rule.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's uniform-in-all-larger-sample-sizes spectral convergence claim is false even in finite-dimensional, uniformly bounded situations.
issues.title: A subsequence at selected sample sizes cannot control arbitrary larger sample-size eigenpair selections
issues.why_classification: The universal quantifier over all larger sample sizes must be abandoned or supplemented by substantial spectral-selection architecture.
